comments.why: Geoff Marshall explains the 15-floors tube station sign oddity.
comments.text: This is a great series, and they manage to point out a lot of the oddities of the UK rail system. They also busted my myth that Gloucester station has the longest platform. (It's pretty flipping long though.) Geoff has a bunch of videos about the details of stations or ticket systems. All tube stations have 15 floors: [VIDEO] Heathrow to Upminster for £1.50: [LINK] Oyster Oddities, are you paying too much?: [LINK]

comments.why: Tube stair signs say 15 floors irrespective of height.
comments.text: Meanwhile, on the London Underground, the lengths of all sets of stairs down to platform level are described as "equivalent to 15 floors" irrespective of how high they actually are: [VIDEO]

comments.author: scoot
comments.story: A Nerd’s Way to Walk Up the Stairs (2011)
comments.why: Tube signs claim stairs equal 15 floors regardless of step count.
comments.text: Reminded me of this video [1] talking about the fact that there are signs in London tube stations claiming the stairs are equivalent to 15 floors, regardless of the number of steps. The number of floors is roughly correct for Covent Garden, so I guess it's possible that the original typesetter changed the number of steps, but forgot to change the number of floors. [1] [VIDEO] Incidental anecdote: While searching for this video, which I'd seen a year or so ago, I googled "tube 15 floors sign", but didn't see a reference to it, so I opened YouTube instead, and there, in recommended videos, was a video about the tube... by the same person that made the video above. It was a short hop to find the correct video. It had never occurred to me that Google personalize youtube searches based on your google searches.
